definitions.explanation: reading something while skipping over parts, either to save time or because of lack of interest in certain sections

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}がなかったので{飛|と}ばし{読|よ}みした。
examples.english: I skimmed through it because I didn't have time.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{小説|しょうせつ}だったので、{途中|とちゅう}から{飛|と}ばし{読|よ}みしてしまった。
examples.english: It was a long novel, so I ended up skimming through it from partway.

notes:
A compound of {飛|と}ばす (to skip) and {読|よ}み (reading). Describes the act of reading while intentionally skipping sections. Can be used as a noun or with する as a verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {飛|と}ばし{読|よ}みする: to skim, to skip-read
- {飛|と}ばし{読|よ}みで{済|す}ませる: to get by with skimming

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {斜|なな}め{読|よ}み: skimming — literally "diagonal reading," a similar concept but implies scanning quickly rather than skipping sections
- {速読|そくどく}: speed reading — a systematic technique for reading quickly, not skipping content
- {拾|ひろ}い{読|よ}み: selective reading — picking out specific parts to read

USAGE:
Often carries a slightly negative connotation, implying that the reader did not give the text proper attention. In contrast, {速読|そくどく} is seen as a positive skill.
